output.summary: The referenced analysis (run_validity VALID, analysis_coverage COMPLETE) reports a BOUNDED capacity bound on load axis "users": lower_inclusive 237, upper_exclusive 357, derived from per-window latency checks (rule "latency", response_time_p95_ms <= 250 ms). Step-1 (target 120 users) PASS (p95 140 ms), step-2 (target 240) PASS (p95 140 ms), step-3 (target 360) FAIL (p95 420 ms). The run-level policy verdict is NO_POLICY and the capacity policy verdict is NO_POLICY; this deterministic verdict is preserved and is not a PASS. capacity_knee is null with KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED (fixed product limitation). Load-generator diagnostic guards (CPU threshold 0.85) PASS in all three windows with generator CPU around 0.41-0.45 ratio. Clock alignment is not_verified_by_core. Advice focuses on: verifying clocks, refining the 237-357 user boundary with intermediate steps, collecting SUT-side telemetry (absent from this analysis), and configuring applicable capacity/SLA rules only if a PASS/FAIL capacity verdict is desired - without altering the diagnostic generator guard.

hypotheses.observation: In window stage-3, policy check for rule "latency" reports observed response_time_p95_ms 420 versus threshold 250 with status FAIL, while the same check reported 140 (PASS) in stage-1 and stage-2 windows; the capacity summary records stage-3 verdict FAIL at verified_bound_load 357 users.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Increasing the target load from 240 users (stage-2) to 360 users (stage-3) pushed p95 latency above the 250 ms target in the stage-3 window. Whether this is a saturation-driven cause is a hypothesis, not proven by the cited evidence.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with intermediate load steps between 237 and 357 users and compare per-window p95 latency to the 250 ms threshold to locate the load level where the breach occurs.

hypotheses.observation: The generator diagnostic guard (rule generator-cpu-guard, threshold 0.85) reports PASS in all three windows; the stage-3 generator CPU resource summary shows mean 0.43, max 0.45 (ratio), with 30/30 observed cells and no gaps.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Load-generator CPU was well below the guard threshold during the failing window, so generator CPU saturation is not supported as the cause of the stage-3 failure; the bottleneck may be downstream on the system under test, whose resource data is not present in this analysis.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Collect SUT CPU/memory/queue telemetry for the stage-3 window and compare it with generator CPU series during a rerun to test the downstream saturation hypothesis.

hypotheses.observation: The resource binding reports clock_alignment "not_verified_by_core" for the evaluation window, with run and evaluation epochs spanning 1767225600000 to 1767226500500.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: If clocks between the load generator and system under test are not aligned, timestamps around the stage-3 breach and any implied temporal ordering (lead/lag) cannot be treated as reliable; an unverified clock relationship cannot support a temporal causal hypothesis.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock synchronization across all involved hosts before interpreting the stage-2 to stage-3 transition as a causal event in a rerun.

hypotheses.observation: The capacity summary and run facts report policy_verdict NO_POLICY (reasons empty) even though a BOUNDED bound (237-357 users) is present; each window policy summary reports resource_verdict NO_POLICY while business verdicts are PASS/PASS/FAIL.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: No applicable capacity policy (required capacity value, or a resource rule with effect sla per stage) produced a capacity verdict in this run, so the product reports NO_POLICY for the policy verdict; the bound itself is still derived and valid. Missing policy is not a pass.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Confirm the capacity policy configuration (required capacity value and per-stage SLA rules for the SUT, not the generator guard) and re-evaluate if a capacity PASS/FAIL verdict is desired.

hypotheses.observation: The overall metric summary reports error_count 0 and error_rate_ratio 0/3601 with p95 417 ms and p99 420 ms; the stage-3 window policy check reports p95 420 ms (FAIL against 250 ms).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The recorded failure is latency-only in this run: zero errors do not demonstrate absence of a problem, and error behavior at loads above the failing step was not measured.
hypotheses.recommended_check: In a rerun, extend loads just above 357 users and record error rate alongside latency to test whether errors emerge with further load increase.

recommendations.action: Verify clock synchronization between the load generator and the system under test before interpreting any temporal or causal relationship around the stage-3 failure.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence reports clock_alignment "not_verified_by_core"; without verified clocks, lead/lag ordering and temporal causal hypotheses are unsupported.

recommendations.action: Rerun with intermediate load targets between 237 and 357 users (for example 280, 320, 350) and evaluate per-window p95 latency against the 250 ms threshold.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence shows PASS at 237 users (p95 140 ms) and FAIL at 357 users (p95 420 ms), so the exact boundary within the BOUNDED range is not measured.

recommendations.action: Instrument the system under test and collect per-window resource telemetry alongside the generator metrics during a rerun.
recommendations.rationale: Generator CPU stayed around 0.41-0.45 ratio with a passing diagnostic guard (0.85 threshold); a downstream saturation explanation for the stage-3 latency breach requires SUT-side data that is absent from this analysis.

recommendations.action: If a capacity PASS/FAIL verdict is desired, provide the required capacity value and applicable per-stage SLA rules (resource rules with effect sla for the SUT); keep the generator guard diagnostic and do not change its effect to sla, binding, or enforcing.
recommendations.rationale: The run-level policy verdict is NO_POLICY; per product rules a missing policy or missing required capacity stays NO_POLICY and is not a PASS. The generator guard is diagnostic by contract.

recommendations.action: Inspect the load-generator resource series around stage transitions for anomalies beyond CPU (for example gaps or metric issues) before relying on the rerun results.
recommendations.rationale: The diagnostic guard passed (CPU 0.41-0.45 vs 0.85 threshold) in all windows, but a passing diagnostic guard does not prove the generator perfectly represented load; its effect is diagnostic by contract.

caveats: Clock alignment is not_verified_by_core (evidence/2); no temporal/causal ordering is supported by the evidence until clocks are verified.

capacity_knee is null with knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. This is a fixed product limitation, not a run defect; it does not invalidate the BOUNDED bound, and no knee detector should be implemented or enabled.

The deterministic run-level policy verdict NO_POLICY is preserved exactly and must not be read as PASS; the stage-3 window FAIL (latency rule) and the NO_POLICY capacity/policy verdict are separate verdicts at different scopes.

The overall metric summary (whole run: 3601 samples, p95 417 ms, p99 420 ms, error_count 0) and per-window policy checks (stage-3 p95 420 ms) are different scopes (run vs window) and are not inconsistent; they should not be compared as the same measurement.
upper_exclusive 357 users is derived from a single failing step (stage-3); uncertainty about the exact boundary between 237 and 357 users is not quantified.
No system-under-test resource metrics are present in the evidence; downstream saturation explanations are untested hypotheses.

No required capacity value is present in the input, so no capacity PASS/FAIL comparison against the 237-357 bound was produced; the NO_POLICY verdict does not indicate a healthy or passing capacity result.
error_count 0 and error_rate 0 do not prove absence of degradation, since stage-3 p95 already exceeded the 250 ms threshold.
The analysis covers a single run; load tests are subject to run-to-run variability.
